questions.q: When is a mock expectation such as $mock->expects(self::once())->method('x') actually verified?

a.t: Automatically during the test's teardown, by PHPUnit's mock verification
Immediately, the moment the mocked method is (or is not) called
Only if you explicitly call $mock->verify() at the end
At the start of the next test method

questions.exp: A mock records its expectations and PHPUnit verifies them at teardown; an unmet expectation (e.g. never called when once() was required) then fails the test. This is exactly what distinguishes a mock from a stub, which asserts nothing. There is no manual verify() call in normal usage.

questions.q: Why can self::getContainer()->get() return a private service in a test?

a.t: It returns the special test container (test.service_container) that exposes private/non-shared services
All services become public in the test environment
It uses reflection to bypass service visibility
Private services are compiled as public only for WebTestCase

questions.exp: The test environment (framework.test: true) compiles a TestContainer that keeps references to used private/non-shared services so tests can fetch and replace them. static::$kernel->getContainer() does not.

questions.q: How are WebTestCase and KernelTestCase related?

a.t: WebTestCase extends KernelTestCase, adding the HTTP client (createClient())

questions.exp: WebTestCase adds the KernelBrowser client on top of the kernel-booting KernelTestCase. Use KernelTestCase when you need only the container.

questions.q: How many times may createClient() be called within a single test?
questions.exp: Only one kernel/client may be booted per test; calling createClient() again throws a LogicException.

questions.q: You must test a service that needs the container but sends no HTTP requests. Which base class fits best?

a.t: KernelTestCase — boots the kernel and exposes the container, without an HTTP client
WebTestCase — because only it can access the container
PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase — the container is available by default

questions.exp: KernelTestCase boots the kernel and gives you self::getContainer() with no browser. WebTestCase adds the HTTP client and is reserved for tests that make requests; a plain TestCase boots no kernel at all.

questions.q: Which utility tests a console command's output and exit code without a real terminal?

a.t: CommandTester — call execute([...]) then getDisplay() and getStatusCode()

questions.exp: Symfony\Component\Console\Tester\CommandTester wraps a single command: execute() supplies input, then getDisplay() returns captured output and getStatusCode() the exit code. ApplicationTester covers the whole app.

questions.q: Given config/packages/test/framework.yaml containing `framework: { test: true }`, what does the `test: true` flag enable?

a.t: The test.client (KernelBrowser) service and the special test container that exposes private services
Only automatic following of redirects for every request
The web profiler toolbar in the browser
Making every private service public across all environments

questions.exp: framework.test: true registers the test.client service (returned by createClient()) and triggers the compiler passes that build the TestContainer exposing used private/non-shared services. Without it, createClient() cannot find test.client. It does not toggle redirect following (a client method) nor the profiler, and it only affects the test environment.

questions.q: What does static::createClient() do to the kernel before returning the client?

a.t: It reboots the kernel so the test starts from fresh container state
It leaves any previously booted kernel untouched and reuses it
It compiles the container from scratch on every request rather than at boot
It permanently disables kernel rebooting for the whole test

questions.exp: createClient() boots (or reboots) the kernel before handing back the KernelBrowser, guaranteeing clean state. The client also reboots the kernel after each request unless you call disableReboot(). It does not reuse a stale kernel, and it does not disable rebooting by default — that is an explicit opt-out.

questions.q: True or False: WebTestCase is a subclass of KernelTestCase, and its only substantive addition is the HTTP client.
questions.exp: WebTestCase extends KernelTestCase; the browser client (createClient() returning a KernelBrowser) is what it adds on top of the kernel-booting and container-access behaviour it inherits. If you do not need HTTP, use KernelTestCase directly.

questions.q: A private service is never injected anywhere. In the test environment it is…

a.t: Still removed — the test container only keeps services that are actually used
Available only after calling bootKernel(['debug' => true])

questions.exp: Unused private services are optimised away even in the test container; only used private/non-shared services remain reachable.

questions.q: To swap a real service for a mock before making a request in a functional test, you should…

a.t: Fetch the test container with self::getContainer() and call ->set('service.id', $mock) before the request
Reassign the property on the kernel's compiled container
Edit config/services.yaml from within the test
Mocks cannot replace services in functional tests

questions.exp: The test container returned by self::getContainer() allows ->set() to override a (used) service with a double. Do this before issuing the request so the kernel uses the replacement.

questions.q: What builds the TestContainer (id test.service_container) that keeps otherwise-private services reachable?

a.t: Compiler passes enabled by framework.test: true (the TestServiceContainer weak/real-ref passes)
A runtime call to Container::compile() inside KernelTestCase::getContainer()
Reflection performed by getContainer() each time it is called
The web profiler bundle registering every service as public

questions.exp: When framework.test: true, dedicated compiler passes (TestServiceContainerWeakRefPass / RealRefPass) build a second container, TestContainer (test.service_container), that retains references to used private/non-shared services. It is a compile-time construct, not runtime reflection, and unused private services are still removed.

questions.q: A test does: $client = static::createClient(); then self::getContainer()->set(PaymentGateway::class, $mock); then $client->request('POST', '/checkout'); — but the real gateway still runs. What is the most likely fix?

a.t: Call $client->disableReboot() before set(), so the replacement survives the reboot that createClient triggers on the next request
Call set() again after the request

questions.exp: By default the kernel reboots (rebuilding a fresh container) around requests, discarding any set() replacement. disableReboot() keeps the container — and your mock — alive across the request. Calling set() after the request is too late; the class already has visibility (getContainer exposes it); and $kernel->getContainer() hides private services entirely.

questions.q: How do you access the test container in a modern Symfony 8 test?

a.t: self::getContainer() — the old static::$container property was removed

questions.exp: The historical static::$container property is gone; call the self::getContainer() method, which returns the TestContainer. $this->container does not exist on the base test classes, and static::$kernel->getContainer() returns the normal container where private services are hidden.

questions.q: Your controller depends on the current time and an external SMS gateway. What is the best testing approach?

a.t: Replace only the boundaries — swap in a MockClock via ClockInterface and a gateway double — keeping the rest of the graph real
Mock every collaborator the controller touches, including the class under test
Use insulate() so the real gateway and real clock run in a subprocess
Avoid the container and instantiate the controller manually with all-null dependencies

questions.exp: Replace only external boundaries you must not hit (SMS) or must make deterministic (time via injected ClockInterface + MockClock), leaving the rest of the wiring real so the test proves integration. Mocking everything tests nothing; insulate() runs a subprocess and would still call the real gateway; hand-instantiating with nulls abandons the point of a functional test.

questions.q: What does $client->request('GET', '/') return?
questions.exp: Navigation methods return a Crawler over the response DOM. Fetch the response object with $client->getResponse().

questions.q: By default, after a controller returns a 302 redirect, the test client…

a.t: Stops on the redirect so you can assert the Location, until you call followRedirect()

questions.exp: Auto-follow is off by default. Use followRedirect() to follow the last redirect once, or followRedirects() to toggle auto-following.

questions.q: Which method keeps a service replaced via getContainer()->set() alive across multiple requests?
questions.exp: By default the kernel reboots after each request, discarding replacements. disableReboot() preserves the container between requests.

questions.q: A test calls $client->followRedirect() and gets a LogicException. What is the cause?

a.t: The last response was not a redirect (no 3xx / Location to follow)
followRedirect() may only be called inside setUp()
The css-selector component is not installed
The profiler was not enabled before the request

questions.exp: followRedirect() follows the last redirect once; if the previous response was not a 3xx there is nothing to follow and it throws a LogicException. It is unrelated to setUp(), css-selector, or the profiler. Assert the redirect first (assertResponseRedirects) before following it.

questions.q: What is the difference between $client->followRedirect() and $client->followRedirects()?

a.t: followRedirect() follows the last redirect once; followRedirects() toggles automatic following for subsequent requests
They are aliases for the same behaviour
followRedirect() toggles auto-follow; followRedirects() follows exactly one redirect
followRedirects() follows all pending redirects immediately for the current response only

questions.exp: followRedirect() (singular) acts once on the last redirect. followRedirects(true|false) (plural) switches auto-following on or off for the rest of the test. Swapping their meaning is a classic exam trap; followRedirects() is a mode toggle, not a one-shot action.

questions.q: What is the signature of KernelBrowser::submitForm()?
questions.exp: You identify the submit button by its text/name/id/value first, then pass the field values and optionally the HTTP method. submitForm() locates the enclosing form for you; if you already hold a Form object, use submit($form).

questions.q: How does the KernelBrowser actually perform a request?

a.t: It converts the BrowserKit request to an HttpFoundation request and calls HttpKernel::handle() in-process — no real network
It opens a real TCP socket to a running web server
It shells out to curl for each request
It renders templates directly, bypassing routing and controllers

questions.exp: KernelBrowser extends AbstractBrowser; doRequest() builds an HttpFoundation Request and passes it straight to HttpKernel::handle(), so the whole stack (routing, controllers, security) runs in-process with no network. The browser keeps a cookie jar and history from the responses.

questions.q: $crawler->filter('div.item') requires which component to be installed?

a.t: None — CSS support is built into DomCrawler

questions.exp: filter() converts the CSS selector to XPath via CssSelectorConverter, so the css-selector component is required. filterXPath() works without it.

questions.q: $crawler->filter('.missing')->text() throws an InvalidArgumentException. Why, and how do you avoid it?

a.t: text() reads the first node and throws on an empty set; pass a default: ->text('')
text() always throws; you must use html() instead
The selector syntax is invalid; only XPath is allowed in text()
text() requires the browser-kit component that is missing

questions.exp: Node-reading methods (text(), attr(), html(), nodeName()) operate on the first matched node and throw when the Crawler is empty, unless you supply a default argument, e.g. text(''). The selector is valid CSS and browser-kit is unrelated; html() would throw identically on an empty set.

questions.q: Which Crawler methods return a NEW Crawler (a subset) rather than reading a scalar value? (choose 3)
questions.exp: The Crawler is immutable: filter(), filterXPath(), first()/last()/eq() all return a new Crawler holding the matched subset. text() and attr() instead read a scalar from the first node (and throw on an empty set without a default), so they are not node-set operations.

questions.q: Internally, how does Crawler::filter() evaluate a CSS selector?

a.t: It converts the CSS to XPath via CssSelectorConverter, then delegates to filterXPath()
It matches CSS against the DOM directly using a native querySelectorAll binding
It compiles the CSS to a regular expression over the raw HTML
It sends the selector to the browser-kit engine for evaluation

questions.exp: filter() uses Symfony\Component\CssSelector\CssSelectorConverter to turn the CSS selector into an XPath expression and then calls filterXPath(); this is why the css-selector component is required for filter() but not for filterXPath(). There is no regex-over-HTML or browser-kit involvement.

questions.q: $crawler->selectButton('Save')->form(['title' => 'x']) returns…

a.t: A Form pre-filled with the page's current values, with 'title' overridden
A raw array of POST data
A brand-new empty Form with only 'title' set

questions.exp: form() builds a Symfony\Component\DomCrawler\Form seeded from the DOM's existing field values; the array argument overrides just the fields you name, leaving the rest at their rendered defaults. It is not a plain array, a Response, nor an empty form.

questions.q: To follow an anchor with $client->click(), you first obtain a Link with…
questions.exp: selectLink() matches anchors by their visible text (or image alt), and ->link() builds a DomCrawler\Link you pass to $client->click(). There is no href() or getLink() convenience returning a Link, and Link is not constructed directly from a Crawler in tests.

questions.q: For which HTTP status codes does assertResponseIsSuccessful() pass?
questions.exp: It asserts the response is in the successful (2xx) range. Use assertResponseStatusCodeSame(n) to check an exact code.

questions.q: Which assertion checks that an element's text is exactly equal (not a substring)?
questions.exp: The ...Same variant requires an exact match; ...Contains checks a substring.

questions.q: What does the WebTestCase helper assertResponseIsSuccessful() verify?

a.t: That the last response has a 2xx status code
That the response body is non-empty
That the response is exactly 200 OK
That the response is a redirect

questions.exp: assertResponseIsSuccessful() passes for any 2xx status. These assertResponse*/assertSelector* helpers come from the BrowserKit/DomCrawler assertion traits mixed into WebTestCase; assertSelectorTextContains() checks a CSS-selected element's text.

questions.q: After a POST that returns a 302, a test does assertSelectorTextContains('h1', 'Welcome') and it fails even though the target page has that heading. Why?

a.t: The current DOM is the redirect (302) page, not the target; you must followRedirect() first
assertSelectorTextContains cannot be used after a POST request
The response status must be asserted before any selector assertion

questions.exp: Redirects are not followed automatically, so the Crawler still holds the (near-empty) 302 response, not the destination page. Calling followRedirect() before the selector assertion loads the target DOM. The assertion works fine after POST and does not depend on a prior status assertion.

questions.q: What does assertResponseRedirects() with no arguments assert?

a.t: Only that the response is a redirect (3xx) — pass a target URL and/or code to be specific
That the response redirects specifically to '/' with a 302
That the redirect has already been followed
That the response is a successful 2xx

questions.exp: With no arguments it merely checks the response is a 3xx redirect. Provide assertResponseRedirects('/target', 302) to also assert the Location and/or the exact status. It does not follow the redirect nor assert success.

questions.q: Which of these are real WebTestCase assertion helpers? (choose 3)
questions.exp: assertResponseStatusCodeSame, assertRouteSame and assertResponseHasCookie all exist in the BrowserKit/WebTest assertion traits. There is no assertResponseBodyEquals (use getResponse()->getContent() with a PHPUnit string assertion) nor assertControllerSame helper.

questions.q: A form submission with invalid data re-renders the form with HTTP 422. Which assertion best expresses "the response is a 422 Unprocessable Content"?
questions.exp: assertResponseIsUnprocessable() is the dedicated helper for a 422 status, the conventional code for a form redisplayed with validation errors. assertResponseIsSuccessful() would fail (422 is not 2xx), redirects apply to 3xx, and asserting an error element checks content, not the status.

questions.q: When must $client->enableProfiler() be called?

a.t: Before the request whose profile you want to read
Never — profiling is always on in the test environment

questions.exp: enableProfiler() opts the next request into profiling; calling it after the request collects nothing and getProfile() returns false.

questions.q: The recommended way to assert that an email was sent in a functional test is…

a.t: Parsing the response HTML for the email body

questions.exp: WebTestCase provides mailer assertions backed by the mailer data collector, so you rarely touch the raw collector.

questions.q: $client->getProfile() when profiling was not enabled returns…
questions.exp: getProfile() returns boolean false (not null, not an empty Profile, and it does not throw) when no profile was collected — typically because enableProfiler() was not called before the request. Guard with assertNotFalse($profile) before reading collectors.

questions.q: In the test environment, framework.profiler.collect defaults to…

a.t: false — profiles are collected only for requests opted in with enableProfiler()
true — every request is profiled automatically
true, but only for redirect responses
It cannot be configured in the test environment

questions.exp: The test profiler config sets collect: false for speed, so profiling is off unless a test calls enableProfiler() before the request. It is fully configurable and is not limited to redirects.

questions.q: A test does: $client->request('GET', '/'); $client->enableProfiler(); $profile = $client->getProfile(); — what is $profile?

a.t: false — enableProfiler() was called after the request, so nothing was collected
A populated Profile for the GET / request
null, because enableProfiler() resets the profile
A Profile containing only the time collector

questions.exp: enableProfiler() opts in the NEXT request; here it runs after the only request, so that request was never profiled and getProfile() returns false. The call order must be enableProfiler() then request() then getProfile().

questions.q: You need to assert which route matched and how long a request took — data not visible in the HTML. What do you do?

a.t: enableProfiler() before the request, then read $profile->getCollector('request') and getCollector('time')
Parse the rendered HTML for a hidden debug comment
Use assertRouteSame() and assertResponseIsSuccessful() only — collectors are unnecessary
Call insulate() so the profiler data is serialized back to the test

questions.exp: The profiler exposes internals through named data collectors (request, time, events, mailer). Enable it before the request, then read the collectors from the Profile. assertRouteSame covers the route but not the duration; insulate() actually removes in-process profiler access.

questions.q: What is the second argument of static::createClient()?

a.t: An array of default server parameters (the $_SERVER bag)
An array of request headers as raw strings
A list of routes to register

questions.exp: createClient(array $options, array $server) — the second array models server parameters (HTTP_* headers, HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER, etc.).

questions.q: To simulate an 'Accept: application/json' request header via server parameters you set…
questions.exp: Request headers become HTTP_-prefixed server parameters. CONTENT_TYPE, HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW are the unprefixed exceptions.

questions.q: What does $client->loginUser($user) do?

a.t: Authenticates the session with the given UserInterface, skipping the login form
Submits the login form with the user's credentials
Creates the user record in the database
Returns a signed JWT for the user

questions.exp: loginUser() injects a security token for a real user object so you can test authorized behaviour without driving the login form.

questions.q: What is the effect of $client->insulate()?

a.t: Each request runs in a separate PHP subprocess, so in-process profiler/container access is lost
The same kernel instance is reused forever

questions.exp: Insulated requests run in a fresh subprocess to isolate global state, at the cost of losing in-process access to the profiler and container.

questions.q: Which server parameters are NOT written with the HTTP_ prefix? (choose 3)
questions.exp: Following CGI conventions, request headers are exposed as HTTP_<NAME>, but CONTENT_TYPE, HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW are special-cased with no prefix. HTTP_ACCEPT and HTTP_X_REQUESTED_WITH are ordinary headers and keep the prefix.

questions.q: A test writes $client->request('GET', '/admin', ['PHP_AUTH_USER' => 'admin', 'PHP_AUTH_PW' => 'secret']) and authentication fails. What is wrong?

a.t: Server params are the 5th argument of request(); the 3rd is $parameters (query/POST). The auth belongs in $server
Basic auth cannot be tested with the client at all
You must call loginUser() instead; server params never carry credentials

questions.exp: request(string $method, string $uri, array $parameters = [], array $files = [], array $server = [], ...): the credentials were passed as $parameters (query/POST data) instead of the 5th $server argument. PHP_AUTH_USER is correctly unprefixed, and Basic auth is testable via server params — the position is the bug.

questions.q: $client->loginUser($user) has no effect (the page still redirects to /login). What is a likely cause?

a.t: There is no configured firewall for the path, or the wrong firewall name was targeted, so no token context is stored
loginUser() only works after calling enableProfiler()
The user must be persisted with the profiler enabled
loginUser() requires insulate() to propagate the token
You must also submit the login form afterwards

questions.exp: loginUser() stores a pre-authenticated token in the session for a firewall; it needs a real UserInterface and a properly configured firewall covering the requested path (and, for multiple firewalls, the correct firewall name). It is independent of the profiler and insulate(), and its whole point is to skip the login form.

questions.q: static::createClient(['debug' => false], ['HTTPS' => true, 'HTTP_HOST' => 'api.example.com']) configures what?

a.t: Kernel boot options (debug off) plus default server params (HTTPS + host) applied to every request from this client
Two sets of request headers merged into one request only
The environment name 'false' and a route host constraint
A single request to https://api.example.com issued immediately

questions.exp: The first array is kernel options (environment/debug); the second is default server parameters merged into every subsequent request(). No request is sent yet, 'debug' is a boolean option (not an environment name), and the values are defaults, not a one-off request.

questions.q: Which class must be registered to enable the PHPUnit bridge's deprecation collection and clock/DNS mocking?
questions.exp: The bridge's PHPUnit extension (registered under <extensions><bootstrap .../>) wires the DeprecationErrorHandler, ClockMock and DnsMock.

questions.q: How is SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER supplied to PHPUnit?

a.t: As an environment/server variable (e.g. in phpunit.dist.xml <php>)

questions.exp: It is read from the environment; commonly set via <php><server name="SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER" .../></php> or the shell.

questions.q: Which SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER value makes the build fail on the very first deprecation?
questions.exp: max[total]=0 sets a zero threshold, so any deprecation fails the suite. weak reports without failing, and disabled=1 turns collection off entirely.

questions.q: In phpunit.dist.xml, how is the bridge's extension registered in PHPUnit 11/12?

a.t: It is auto-registered by Composer; no XML entry is needed

questions.exp: PHPUnit 10+ uses the <extensions><bootstrap .../></extensions> mechanism to load the SymfonyExtension. The old <listeners><listener> (SymfonyTestsListener) approach belongs to PHPUnit 9 and earlier; there is no <php><extension> tag, and the extension is not auto-registered.

questions.q: Your test calls sleep(61) expecting it to be instant (mocked), but it actually sleeps. What is missing?

a.t: The test (or class) is not in the time-sensitive group, so ClockMock does not override the time functions
You forgot to call ClockMock::register() manually in every test
sleep() can never be mocked; only microtime() can
SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER must be set to weak for clock mocking

questions.exp: ClockMock only overrides time(), sleep(), microtime(), etc. for tests in the time-sensitive group (#[Group('time-sensitive')]); without that group the real functions run. The extension handles registration, sleep() IS among the mocked functions, and the deprecations helper is unrelated.

questions.q: A service injects Symfony\Component\Clock\ClockInterface. What is the cleanest way to control time in its test?

a.t: Inject a Symfony\Component\Clock\MockClock and advance it, instead of using ClockMock and the time-sensitive group
Put the test in the time-sensitive group and rely on ClockMock overriding global time()
Call sleep() with real durations to advance the clock
Mock ClockInterface with createMock() and return a fixed DateTime once

questions.exp: For code that injects ClockInterface, swapping a MockClock (which you can advance deterministically) is cleaner and needs no group magic. ClockMock + time-sensitive is the tool for legacy code calling global time()/sleep() directly. Real sleep() is slow, and a one-shot createMock stub cannot model advancing time.

questions.q: True or False: the bin/simple-phpunit wrapper is the recommended way to run the suite in Symfony 8.
questions.exp: The legacy simple-phpunit wrapper is deprecated in favour of registering SymfonyExtension in the PHPUnit config and running plain PHPUnit (bin/phpunit). The extension provides the same deprecation collection and clock/DNS mocking without the wrapper.

questions.q: A deprecation triggered deep inside a vendor library's own internals is classified as…
questions.exp: self = your code, direct = a dependency you call directly, indirect = deep inside a dependency's internals, legacy = tests excluded from thresholds.

questions.q: What does SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER=weak do?

a.t: Reports deprecations but never fails the build
Hides deprecations entirely and collects nothing
Fails the build on the first deprecation

questions.exp: weak collects and prints deprecations without enforcing thresholds. disabled=1 turns collection off; max[...] enforces limits.

questions.q: The modern way to silence a single test's expected deprecations is…
questions.exp: Symfony\Bridge\PhpUnit\Attribute\IgnoreDeprecations replaces the old @group legacy for excluding a test's deprecations from the report.

questions.q: Match the deprecation buckets correctly. Which statements are TRUE? (choose 3)

a.t: self = triggered by your own code's namespace
direct = triggered by a dependency you called directly
legacy = deprecations from tests marked legacy, never counted against thresholds
indirect = triggered by your own test setup code
direct = deep inside a dependency's internals

questions.exp: self is your code, direct is a dependency you call directly, indirect is deep inside a dependency's internals, and legacy (marked tests) is excluded from thresholds. The two false options swap direct/indirect and mislabel indirect as your own setup.

questions.q: You want to assert that calling a method emits a specific deprecation. Which is correct in Symfony 8?

a.t: use ExpectUserDeprecationMessageTrait; then $this->expectUserDeprecationMessage('Since app 2.0: ...') before the call

questions.exp: ExpectUserDeprecationMessageTrait::expectUserDeprecationMessage() is the current API for asserting an emitted E_USER_DEPRECATED message. The old ExpectDeprecationTrait::expectDeprecation() and the @expectedDeprecation annotation were removed in Symfony 7.0, and deprecations are not exceptions.

questions.q: What is the difference between weak and disabled=1?

a.t: weak still collects and reports deprecations (just never fails); disabled=1 stops collection entirely
They are identical — both hide deprecations
weak stops collection; disabled=1 reports without failing
weak fails on self deprecations only; disabled=1 fails on all

questions.exp: weak keeps collecting and printing the grouped report but never enforces a threshold, so you retain visibility. disabled=1 turns the handler off so nothing is collected or reported. The pair is a common trap when their behaviours are swapped; neither of them fails the build.

questions.q: A legacy suite emits hundreds of known deprecations, but you want CI to fail only on NEW ones. What do you do?

a.t: Generate a baseline (baselineFile=...&generateBaseline=true), commit it, then run with baselineFile=... so only new deprecations fail
Set disabled=1 permanently so nothing is reported
Add #[IgnoreDeprecations] to every test in the suite
Set weak so the build never turns red

questions.exp: A baseline records currently-known deprecations to a JSON file that later runs ignore, so only new deprecations fail the build — and you shrink it over time. disabled=1 and weak both remove the safety net for new deprecations, and blanket #[IgnoreDeprecations] hides everything, including regressions.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are true about the test client returned by static::createClient()? (select all that apply)

a.t: It is a KernelBrowser (extending AbstractBrowser) that calls the kernel in-process, not over the network
It does not follow redirects by default; you must call followRedirect() or followRedirects()
request() returns a Crawler; the Response is fetched separately via $client->getResponse()
It performs real HTTP requests against a running web server
request() returns the Response object directly

questions.exp: The client is a KernelBrowser hitting the kernel in-process with a cookie jar and history, so no web server or network round-trip is involved. Navigation methods like request() return a Crawler — the Response must be read via getResponse() — and redirects are only followed after calling followRedirect() (once) or followRedirects() (toggle), never automatically.

questions.q: Which statements about configuring the test client are correct? (select all that apply)

a.t: Request headers are passed as HTTP_-prefixed server parameters (e.g. HTTP_ACCEPT), while HTTPS, PHP_AUTH_USER and PHP_AUTH_PW stay unprefixed
loginUser() authenticates a real UserInterface instance without going through the login form
insulate() runs each request in a separate process, so you lose in-process profiler/container access
Server parameters are the first argument of createClient(), before the kernel options
loginUser() only needs the username string; the user object is loaded automatically

questions.exp: Headers become HTTP_-prefixed server parameters, with CONTENT_TYPE, HTTPS and PHP_AUTH_* as unprefixed exceptions; loginUser() sets the security token directly from a real UserInterface object, skipping the login form; and insulate() isolates each request in a subprocess at the cost of profiler and container access. createClient() takes ($options, $server), so server parameters are the second argument, and loginUser() requires an actual user object, not just a username.

questions.q: Which statements about the DomCrawler used in functional tests are true? (select all that apply)

a.t: filter() with CSS selectors requires the css-selector component; filterXPath() works without it
The Crawler is immutable: filter() returns a new node set instead of mutating the original
text() and attr() read the first node and throw on an empty set unless a default argument is provided
filterXPath() also requires the css-selector component because XPath is converted to CSS internally
filter() narrows the current Crawler in place and returns $this

questions.exp: CSS selectors are translated to XPath by the css-selector component, so only filter() needs it — filterXPath() speaks the native language directly. Every filtering call returns a new immutable Crawler instance rather than mutating the original, and text()/attr() operate on the first node, throwing on an empty set unless a default value is passed. Nothing converts XPath to CSS; the conversion goes the other way.

questions.q: Which statements about SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER modes are correct? (select all that apply)

a.t: weak keeps collecting and reporting deprecations but never fails the build
disabled=1 turns the handler off entirely, so nothing is collected or reported
A committed baseline file makes only NEW deprecations fail, ignoring the known ones it records
weak and disabled=1 are equivalent — both hide deprecations completely
max[self]=0 fails the build on deprecations from any bucket, including indirect ones

questions.exp: weak still prints the grouped deprecation report and only removes the failure threshold, whereas disabled=1 stops collection completely, so the two are not equivalent. A baseline records currently-known deprecations so later runs fail only on new ones. max[self]=0 constrains only the self bucket — max[total]=0 is the mode that fails on any bucket.

questions.q: Which statements about accessing and replacing services in tests are true? (select all that apply)

a.t: self::getContainer() returns the special test container, which exposes private services that are used somewhere
A service replaced with $container->set() is lost when the kernel reboots between requests, unless you call disableReboot()
static::$kernel->getContainer() exposes the same private services as the test container
The old static::$container property is still the recommended way to get the container
Completely unused private services remain available in the test container

questions.exp: Only the test container from self::getContainer() exposes private services, and only those actually used somewhere — completely unused private services are still optimised away, and $kernel->getContainer() keeps private services hidden. Because the client reboots the kernel between requests, set() replacements disappear unless disableReboot() is called, and the removed static::$container property must not be used.

questions.q: Which statements about WebTestCase response assertions are correct? (select all that apply)

a.t: assertResponseIsSuccessful() passes for any 2xx status code, not only 200
assertSelectorTextContains() checks a substring, while assertSelectorTextSame() requires an exact match
assertResponseRedirects() called without arguments only checks that the response is a redirect (3xx)
assertResponseIsSuccessful() fails unless the status code is exactly 200
Selector-based assertions work without the css-selector component installed

questions.exp: assertResponseIsSuccessful() accepts any 2xx — use assertResponseStatusCodeSame(200) for an exact code. The ...Contains variants match substrings while ...Same demands exact equality, and assertResponseRedirects() with no arguments only verifies a 3xx status (pass a target and/or code to be more specific). Selector assertions use CSS selectors, so they do require the css-selector component.

questions.q: Which statements about the Symfony PHPUnit bridge are true? (select all that apply)

a.t: Its features are wired by registering Symfony\Bridge\PhpUnit\SymfonyExtension in the PHPUnit configuration
Clock and DNS mocking are opt-in per test via the time-sensitive and dns-sensitive groups
SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER is an environment/server variable, not a PHPUnit CLI flag
Clock mocking is applied automatically to every test once the bridge is installed
Deprecation reporting is tuned with the phpunit --deprecations-helper command-line option

questions.exp: Deprecation collection and clock/DNS mocking only work once the SymfonyExtension is registered in the PHPUnit configuration, and the mocking is opt-in per group (time-sensitive / dns-sensitive) rather than applied globally. Reporting is tuned through the SYMFONY_DEPRECATIONS_HELPER env/server variable; no equivalent PHPUnit CLI flag exists.

questions.q: Which Twig delimiter executes a statement without printing anything?
questions.exp: {% %} runs tags/control flow, {{ }} prints an (escaped) expression, and {# #} is a comment that is stripped at compile time.

questions.q: What does {{ 7 // 2 }} output in Twig?
questions.exp: // is integer (floor) division in Twig; / performs float division and would return 3.5.

questions.q: What is the result of {{ "a" ~ 1 + 1 }}?
questions.exp: + binds tighter than ~, so it evaluates as "a" ~ (1 + 1) => "a" ~ 2 => "a2". ~ is string concatenation, not addition.

questions.q: How do you strip whitespace between HTML tags in current Twig 3.x?
questions.exp: The {% spaceless %} tag was removed in Twig 3; use the spaceless filter via {% apply spaceless %} (or the {{- -}} whitespace modifiers).

questions.q: For {{ user.name }}, in which order does Twig try to resolve the attribute?

a.t: getName() first, then the public property, then array access

questions.exp: Twig's attribute resolver tries array/index access first, then a public property, then method calls name(), getName(), isName() and hasName(). Force pure array access with user['name'] and dynamic names with attribute(user, key). A missing attribute yields null unless strict_variables is on.

questions.q: What does {{ -5|abs }} produce, given filters bind tighter than any operator?

a.t: An error about applying a filter to a negative literal

questions.exp: The pipe binds tighter than the unary minus, so the expression is -(5|abs) = -(5) = -5, not (-5)|abs. Wrap in parentheses — (-5)|abs — to get 5. This tight binding of filters is a recurring exam trap.

questions.q: How is a Twig template turned into something executable, and what is cached?

a.t: It is lexed, parsed and compiled to a PHP class extending Twig\Template, cached under var/cache
It is interpreted line by line on every request, nothing is cached
It is transpiled to JavaScript and cached in the browser
It is stored as a serialized AST and re-parsed each request

questions.exp: Twig is a compiler: Environment::render() runs lex -> parse -> compile, emitting a PHP class extending Twig\Template whose doDisplay() contains echo statements. It is written once to var/cache/<env>/twig via FilesystemCache and reused, so runtime parsing cost is zero after the first compile.

questions.q: With strict_variables enabled, what happens when you print an undefined variable {{ missing }}?

a.t: It throws a RuntimeError; without strict_variables it would silently print empty
It prints empty regardless of strict_variables
It throws only in the prod environment

questions.exp: With strict_variables on (recommended in dev), an undefined variable throws so typos surface early. In lenient mode (the default) it prints an empty string. Note a variable that resolves to null still prints empty even under strict_variables — strict_variables catches undefined, not null.

questions.q: True or false: {# ... #} comments are removed at compile time and never reach the browser.
questions.exp: Twig {# #} comments are stripped during compilation and produce no output, unlike HTML <!-- --> comments which are sent to the client. Use {# #} for template notes you do not want leaking to users.

questions.q: In Symfony, how is the default auto-escaping strategy chosen for a template?

a.t: Guessed from the template file extension (e.g. .html.twig => html)

questions.exp: TwigBundle configures autoescape to 'name', using FileExtensionEscapingStrategy::guess() so .html.twig escapes as html, .js.twig as js, .txt.twig not at all.

questions.q: A value is placed inside <script>const x = "...";</script>. Which escape filter is correct?
questions.exp: A JavaScript string context requires the 'js' strategy; HTML escaping does not neutralise the characters dangerous in JS.

questions.q: What does {% autoescape false %} ... {% endautoescape %} do?

a.t: Disables auto-escaping inside the block (use for trusted content only)
Escapes the content as plain text
Escapes the content as a URL

questions.exp: It turns escaping off within the block, exactly like piping every value through |raw. Only use it for trusted/sanitised content.

questions.q: Which escaping filter is required for a value used inside an HTML attribute?
questions.exp: Attribute context needs the stricter html_attr encoder, which escapes spaces, =, backticks and other characters that html escaping leaves untouched.

questions.q: How much of a .txt.twig template's {{ }} output is auto-escaped by Symfony's default strategy?

a.t: None — the .txt.twig extension maps to no escaping (false)
All values are html-escaped like any other template
Twig throws because .txt.twig has no strategy

questions.exp: FileExtensionEscapingStrategy::guess() maps .txt.twig to false (no escaping), which is correct because plain-text output has no HTML context. The trap is assuming escaping is always html — it is chosen per extension, and .txt.twig escapes nothing.

questions.q: A template renders user-submitted comment HTML with {{ comment|raw }}. What is the risk?

a.t: Stored XSS: |raw disables escaping, so untrusted markup/scripts run unfiltered
It only affects performance, not security
Twig sanitizes |raw output automatically in prod

questions.exp: |raw marks the value safe and skips auto-escaping, so any <script> in a user comment executes — a classic stored XSS hole. Only use |raw on HTML you generated or ran through the HtmlSanitizer component; never on raw user input.

questions.q: At which point is auto-escaping applied to a value?

a.t: At print time on {{ }}, via EscaperExtension adding an implicit |escape
When the variable is assigned with {% set %}
When the controller passes the variable to the template
During template compilation, once, on the source string

questions.exp: EscaperExtension inserts an implicit |escape(strategy) on every {{ }} output node that is not already marked safe — escaping happens when a value is printed, not when it is set. So {% set x = untrusted %} stores it raw; the escaping occurs only when you later print {{ x }}.

questions.q: Which PHP function backs Twig's default 'html' escaping strategy?
questions.exp: The EscaperRuntime maps 'html' to htmlspecialchars() with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE (encoding single and double quotes and substituting invalid code units). html_attr uses a stricter attribute encoder, js uses \\xNN hex, css uses CSS hex and url uses rawurlencode — each context has its own encoder because escaping is context-specific.

questions.q: In a .html.twig file, what does {{ 'hi' }} render to the browser?
questions.exp: Auto-escaping (html strategy for .html.twig) converts the angle brackets to entities, so the literal markup is displayed as text rather than rendered as bold. To output real markup you would need |raw (only for trusted content).

questions.q: True or false: in Symfony, Twig output escaping is enabled by default.
questions.exp: Auto-escaping is on by default (autoescape: name) as a baseline XSS defence; every {{ }} is escaped for its context unless the value is marked safe or passed through |raw. You opt out per value, not opt in.

questions.q: How many templates can a single template extend in Twig?
questions.exp: Twig uses single vertical inheritance. For reusing blocks from several templates (horizontal reuse), use the {% use %} tag instead.

questions.q: Inside an overridden block, what does {{ parent() }} render?

a.t: The parent template's version of that same block

questions.exp: parent() outputs the content of the same block from the parent template, letting a child extend rather than fully replace it.

questions.q: Which tag provides horizontal reuse of blocks (like a trait)?
questions.exp: {% use %} imports block definitions from another template without setting a parent, and multiple use statements are allowed.

questions.q: What is the difference between {{ parent() }} and {{ block('sidebar') }}?

a.t: parent() renders the parent's version of the current block; block('x') renders block x of the current hierarchy
They are aliases and do the same thing
parent() renders any named block; block('x') renders the whole parent template
block('x') only works in the parent template, parent() only in the child

questions.exp: parent() is contextual — it renders the same block one level up in the inheritance chain. block('name') prints a named block resolved from the current template hierarchy (and block('name', 'other.html.twig') from another template). Confusing the two is a common exam distractor.

questions.q: Why must {% extends %} be the first tag, and what can a child template NOT do?

a.t: A child that extends a parent cannot output markup outside blocks; rendering starts at the root ancestor
Markup outside blocks is allowed and rendered before the parent
extends may appear anywhere; order does not matter
A child can define its own <html> wrapper around the parent

questions.exp: When a template extends another, rendering begins at the root ancestor and walks down, so any top-level text a child writes outside a block is ignored (or errors). extends can be a dynamic expression resolved at runtime, which is why it must be resolvable first. Put all child content inside blocks.

questions.q: How does template inheritance work at the compiled-PHP level?

a.t: Each {% block %} becomes a block_<name>() method; extends makes the child class override the parent's methods
Blocks are stored as strings and concatenated at runtime
The child template is textually copied into the parent before compilation
Inheritance is resolved by regular expressions on the source

questions.exp: Every template compiles to a class extending Twig\Template; a block becomes a block_<name>() method and extends wires up parentage so child methods override parent ones — exactly like PHP method overriding. A block table ($this->blocks) lets an override anywhere in the chain win.

questions.q: What does {% extends request.isXmlHttpRequest ? '_ajax.html.twig' : 'base.html.twig' %} demonstrate?

a.t: extends accepts a dynamic expression, resolved at runtime to choose the parent
A syntax error — extends only accepts a string literal
It extends both templates at once
It includes the ajax template rather than extending it

questions.exp: The parent name in extends can be any expression, evaluated at runtime, so you can pick a layout conditionally (e.g. a bare layout for AJAX requests). This is why extends is resolved at runtime rather than purely at compile time.

questions.q: Which statements about {% use %} are correct? (choose 2)

a.t: It imports block definitions only, not surrounding markup
Multiple use statements are allowed in one template
It sets the template's parent like extends
It can override the parent's <html> skeleton

questions.exp: {% use %} performs horizontal reuse: it pulls in block definitions (like a PHP trait) without setting a parent, and you may use several templates, aliasing name clashes with 'as'. It does not import non-block markup and does not establish inheritance — that is what extends is for.

questions.q: What does app.user return when no one is authenticated?
questions.exp: AppVariable::getUser() reads the token from the token storage and returns its user, or null when there is no authenticated user.

questions.q: Which class backs the Twig `app` global in Symfony?
questions.exp: TwigBundle registers Symfony\Bridge\Twig\AppVariable as the `app` global; its getters expose user, request, session, flashes, etc.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a member of the `app` global?
questions.exp: app exposes user, request, session, flashes, environment, debug, token, locale, current_route and current_route_parameters. There is no app.controller.

questions.q: What does app.environment return?

a.t: The kernel environment string, e.g. 'dev' or 'prod'

questions.exp: app.environment is the kernel environment (dev/prod/test); app.debug is the boolean debug flag. They are unrelated to OS env vars.

questions.q: How do you register a static global string in Twig?

a.t: Under twig.globals in config, or via a GlobalsInterface extension

questions.exp: Declare globals under twig.globals in twig.yaml, or return them from an extension implementing Twig\Extension\GlobalsInterface::getGlobals().

questions.q: In Symfony 8, which expression prints the current user's identifier?
questions.exp: UserInterface exposes getUserIdentifier(), so the Twig accessor is app.user.userIdentifier. The legacy getUsername()/username idiom is gone in modern Symfony. Remember to guard app.user first — it is null for anonymous requests.

questions.q: Which app.* accesses have a side effect? (choose 2)

a.t: app.session — accessing it can start the session
app.flashes — reading flash messages consumes (clears) them
app.environment — pure read, no side effect
app.debug — pure read, no side effect

questions.exp: Accessing app.session may start the session (which can defeat HTTP caching), and reading app.flashes consumes the messages so they are cleared after display — both have side effects. app.environment and app.debug are plain reads with no side effect.

questions.q: You need a global whose value is computed from an injected service. Which approach fits best?

a.t: An extension implementing GlobalsInterface::getGlobals() returning the computed value
A {% set %} at the top of base.html.twig
Hard-coding it in every controller's render() call

questions.exp: GlobalsInterface::getGlobals() lets an extension inject a service and return computed values, resolved lazily when the extension is instantiated. A static YAML twig.globals entry (even '@service') is fine for simple references, but computed/lazy values belong in a GlobalsInterface extension. There is no #[AsGlobal] attribute.

questions.q: A controller passes a variable named `app` to the template. What happens?

a.t: The local variable shadows the global, so app.user etc. refer to the passed value
The global always wins and the local value is ignored
Both are merged into a single object

questions.exp: Globals are merged into the render context, so a local variable of the same name shadows the global. Passing your own `app` variable breaks app.user/app.request access inside that template — avoid reusing reserved global names.

questions.q: Which snippet safely greets an authenticated user and falls back to 'Guest'?
questions.exp: Because app.user is null for anonymous requests, you must guard it before dereferencing. The ternary checks app.user first. Reading app.user.userIdentifier directly throws under strict_variables (and is the classic anonymous-page crash); Guest is a bareword not a string in the third option; app.userIdentifier is not a member.

questions.q: Which attribute registers a custom Twig filter in current Twig 3.x?
questions.exp: Twig 3.x provides Twig\Attribute\AsTwigFilter and AsTwigFunction as an attribute-based alternative to returning TwigFilter/TwigFunction from an AbstractExtension.

questions.q: A custom filter returns 'x' but the page shows escaped text. Why?

a.t: The filter must be declared with the is_safe => ['html'] option
You must call |raw on the input

questions.exp: Filter/function output is auto-escaped unless the TwigFilter/TwigFunction declares is_safe for the relevant context.

questions.q: What does the `default` filter replace?
questions.exp: default(x) substitutes x when the value is undefined, null or empty (unless you pass true as the second argument to only test 'defined').

questions.q: Which statement about filters vs functions is correct?

a.t: A filter is applied with the pipe (value|f) and a function is called by name f(args); date exists as both
Filters and functions are interchangeable syntaxes for the same registration
path() is a filter and lower is a function

questions.exp: value|filter transforms a piped value while function(args) is called by name; they are registered as distinct TwigFilter/TwigFunction objects. A name like date is registered both as a filter (now|date('Y')) and a function (date()). path()/lower are function and filter respectively — the reversed option is wrong.

questions.q: A TwigFilter is declared with needs_environment: true. What changes about the callable?

a.t: Twig passes the Environment as the first argument, shifting the user arguments right
Nothing changes; it is only documentation metadata
The filter can only be used inside {% apply %} blocks
The callable must return a Twig\Environment

questions.exp: needs_environment injects Twig\Environment as the first callable argument (and needs_context injects the render context array), so your declared parameters come after it. Forgetting this argument shift is a common cause of TypeErrors when writing extensions.

questions.q: Which method definition correctly registers a `vat` function via attributes?

a.t: public function vat(float $n): float // auto-detected by name

questions.exp: Twig\Attribute\AsTwigFunction('vat') on a method registers the function; Symfony autoconfiguration wires the class. There is no #[TwigFunction] or #[AsFunction] attribute, and functions are not auto-detected by method name without an attribute or getFunctions() registration.

questions.q: Why put a filter's heavy-dependency logic in a runtime class rather than the extension itself?

a.t: The runtime is lazily instantiated only when the filter is actually used, so heavy services are not built every request
Runtimes are the only way to register a filter in Twig 3

questions.exp: An AbstractExtension is instantiated on every request, so injecting a costly dependency into it slows all requests. Moving the logic to a runtime (RuntimeExtensionInterface / the attribute style) makes it lazy — built only when the filter is invoked. Auto-escaping is unaffected by this choice.

questions.q: Given an empty string, what do {{ ''|default('x') }} and {{ '' ?? 'x' }} produce?

a.t: 'x' and '' — default replaces empty values, ?? only replaces null/undefined
'' and '' — neither treats empty as replaceable
'' and 'x' — default keeps empty, ?? replaces it

questions.exp: The default filter substitutes for undefined, null AND empty values ('', [], false), so ''|default('x') yields 'x'. The ?? operator only replaces null/undefined, so '' ?? 'x' keeps the empty string. This difference is a frequent exam trap.

questions.q: What does the `only` keyword do on an include?

a.t: Restricts the included template's scope to just the `with` variables

questions.exp: By default an include inherits the parent context; adding `only` isolates it so it sees only the variables passed via `with` (plus the app global).

questions.q: Which construct includes a template AND lets you override its blocks?
questions.exp: embed combines include with extends-style block overriding, ideal for configurable components with slots.

questions.q: What does {% include ['a.html.twig', 'b.html.twig'] %} render?

a.t: The first template in the list that exists

questions.exp: Passing an array of names renders the first template that can be loaded, which is handy for theme overrides.

questions.q: With {% include '_card.html.twig' with { title: t } only %}, is the app global still available inside the partial?

a.t: Yes — only isolates the parent's local variables but globals like app remain available
No — only removes everything including globals
Only if you also pass app in the with hash
Globals are never available inside an include

questions.exp: only restricts the include to just the with variables from the caller's local scope, but Twig globals (such as app) are merged into every template's context independently, so app.user etc. still work. Assuming only strips globals is a common misconception.

questions.q: A template exists but throws inside itself. Does `ignore missing` on the include suppress that error?

a.t: No — ignore missing only suppresses LoaderError for a missing template, not errors thrown while rendering an existing one
Yes — ignore missing swallows any error inside the include
It converts the error into an empty string always

questions.exp: ignore missing guards only against the template not being found (LoaderError). Once a template is loaded, any runtime/compile error inside it still propagates. Treating ignore missing as a catch-all is a trap that hides real bugs.

questions.q: What does {{ include('_card.html.twig', { title: t }, with_context = false) }} do?

a.t: Renders the partial with only { title: t } (no parent context) and returns it as a string usable in an expression
Includes the template inline but keeps the full parent context
Throws because the function form does not accept with_context
Renders it only if the template is missing

questions.exp: The include() function returns a string (so it composes in expressions) and takes named options; with_context = false is the function-form equivalent of the only keyword, isolating the partial to the passed variables. Globals remain available.

questions.q: How is an included template handled by Twig internally?

a.t: It is a separate compiled class, loaded via the loader and invoked at runtime — not textually inlined
Its source is pasted into the parent before compilation
It is re-parsed from disk on every render with no caching
It is merged into the parent's single block table

questions.exp: The include tag compiles to a call to Twig\Template::display()/render() on the sub-template, which the FilesystemLoader resolves and which is compiled and cached like any other template. Includes are separate compiled classes invoked at runtime, not inlined text.

questions.q: What is loop.index on the first iteration of a for loop?
questions.exp: loop.index is 1-based; loop.index0 is the 0-based counterpart.

questions.q: When does the `else` clause of a for loop execute?

a.t: When the collection is empty (zero iterations)

questions.exp: {% for ... else ... endfor %} renders the else block only when the loop produced no iterations.

questions.q: How do you skip iterations in a Twig for loop?

a.t: Filter the source, e.g. {% for x in items if x.active %}

questions.exp: Twig has no break/continue by design; filter the iterable inline or use an if inside the body.

questions.q: Why might loop.length and loop.last be unavailable inside a for loop?

a.t: The iterable is not countable (e.g. a bare Generator), so Twig cannot know the total up front
They are only available under strict_variables
They never work in nested loops
They require the collection to be an array of objects

questions.exp: loop.length, loop.last and loop.revindex require a countable iterable (array or Countable/Traversable Twig can count). For a non-countable Generator, Twig cannot determine the total without buffering, so those members may be omitted; loop.index and loop.first are always available.

questions.q: Inside a nested loop, how do you access the outer loop's current index?
questions.exp: loop.parent gives the enclosing loop's context, so loop.parent.loop.index is the outer loop's 1-based index. A bare loop.index inside the inner loop refers to the inner loop only.

questions.q: Which is true about the tests `is null`, `is empty`, and `is defined`?

a.t: is empty is broadest — true for null, false, 0, '' and []; is null is only for null; is defined checks existence
is empty is true only for '' (empty string)
is defined is true only when the value is not null

questions.exp: is defined tests whether the variable exists at all (undefined is not the same as null); is null tests exact null; is empty is the broadest — true for null, false, 0, '' and []. Use is null when you must distinguish "no value" from "empty list", and combine with is defined for maybe-missing variables.

questions.q: What happens with {% for x in items %}...{% else %}Empty{% endfor %} when items is null?

a.t: Zero iterations run and the else block renders 'Empty' (no error in lenient mode)
A RuntimeError because you cannot iterate null
The loop body runs once with x = null

questions.exp: Iterating null in lenient mode is safe — it produces zero iterations and falls through to the for...else block. That makes for...else the natural guard for a possibly-null collection, so you rarely need a wrapping {% if items %}.

questions.q: Which loop iterates a hash by key and value?

a.t: {% for value, key in map %} always

questions.exp: Twig's key/value form is {% for key, value in map %} (key first). There is no foreach tag and no PHP-style => or 'as' syntax in Twig loops.

questions.q: True or false: Twig provides a {% break %} tag to exit a loop early.
questions.exp: Twig deliberately has no break or continue tag to keep templates declarative. Filter the iterable (for x in items if ...) or slice it (items|slice(0, n)) to limit iterations instead.

questions.q: What is the difference between path() and url() in Twig?

a.t: path() returns a relative URL, url() returns an absolute URL
url() is relative, path() is absolute

questions.exp: Both use UrlGeneratorInterface via RoutingExtension; path() uses ABSOLUTE_PATH (relative) and url() uses ABSOLUTE_URL (scheme + host).

questions.q: Given route 'search' => /search, what does path('search', {q: 'x', page: 2}) produce?
questions.exp: Parameters not consumed by the route pattern are appended as the query string.

questions.q: Which Twig extension provides path() and url()?
questions.exp: RoutingExtension wraps the UrlGeneratorInterface and reads the RequestContext to build relative and absolute URLs.

questions.q: You are building an HTML email template with a link back to the site. Which function should you use?

a.t: url() — an email needs an absolute URL (scheme + host); path() yields a relative link that breaks in mail clients
path() — it is shorter and mail clients resolve it against the site
asset() — it produces the right host for emails
Either works identically in an email

questions.exp: When a link leaves the page (emails, RSS, canonical tags, redirects consumed elsewhere) it must be absolute, so use url(). A relative path() link has no host and breaks once opened in a mail client. asset() is for static files, not routes.

questions.q: path('article_show') is called but the route requires a {slug}. What happens at render time?

a.t: The slug defaults to an empty string and the URL renders

questions.exp: The generator throws MissingMandatoryParametersException when a required route parameter is not supplied. (An unknown route name instead throws RouteNotFoundException.) Both surface at render time, not silently.

questions.q: Which UrlGenerator reference types back path() and url() respectively?

a.t: Both use ABSOLUTE_URL, differing only in caching

questions.exp: RoutingExtension calls UrlGenerator::generate() with ABSOLUTE_PATH for path() (a root-relative /path) and ABSOLUTE_URL for url() (scheme + host + path). The generator reads the RequestContext to build the host for absolute URLs.

questions.q: Which snippet builds a 'next page' link for the current route, incrementing page?
questions.exp: app.current_route and app.current_route_parameters expose the active route and its params; merging a new page value onto them and passing to path() rebuilds the current URL with one changed parameter. app.route/app.params are not real members, and + does not merge hashes (~ /merge do).

questions.q: How does render(controller('C::m')) execute the controller?

a.t: As a sub-request through HttpKernel (inline fragment)
As a plain static method call with no request

questions.exp: The InlineFragmentRenderer issues a real HttpKernel sub-request, so the kernel events run again for the fragment.

questions.q: What happens with render_esi() when no ESI-capable reverse proxy is present?

a.t: It transparently falls back to inline rendering

questions.exp: Without a proxy that understands ESI, Symfony degrades render_esi to an inline sub-request so the page still works.

questions.q: Which service selects the fragment renderer for render()/render_esi()?
questions.exp: HttpKernelExtension delegates to FragmentHandler, which picks a FragmentRendererInterface (inline, esi, hinclude) by strategy name.

questions.q: A sidebar just needs variables the parent already has. include or render(controller())?

a.t: include — it is the cheapest option when no extra logic/data is needed
render_esi — fragments should always be cached separately
render_hinclude — load everything asynchronously by default

questions.exp: Each inline embed is a real sub-request with its own overhead. If the fragment only needs data you already have, a plain include is far cheaper. Reserve render(controller()) for fragments that need their own services/data/cache.

questions.q: What does render_hinclude() do differently from inline rendering?

a.t: It emits a placeholder that the browser resolves asynchronously via JavaScript
It renders the fragment inline but caches it in the profiler
It always requires a reverse proxy
It renders nothing until the page reloads

questions.exp: HIncludeFragmentRenderer outputs a placeholder tag resolved by the browser with JavaScript, so the main page renders immediately and the fragment loads asynchronously afterwards. Inline instead blocks on a synchronous sub-request.

questions.q: What is true about kernel events when an inline fragment is rendered?

a.t: The full request lifecycle runs again for the sub-request (kernel.request, kernel.controller, kernel.response, etc.)
No events fire because it is an internal call
Only kernel.response fires for the fragment
The parent request's events are re-dispatched for the fragment

questions.exp: Inline rendering calls HttpKernel::handle(..., SUB_REQUEST), so the whole listener chain (request, controller, response) runs independently for the fragment. The sub-request has its own Request object; parent attributes are not automatically shared.

questions.q: Which config enables direct fragment URLs for ESI/hinclude?

a.t: framework.fragments.enabled: true (with a path), plus framework.esi.enabled: true for ESI
No config is needed; fragment URLs are always public

questions.exp: Embedded controllers are normally reachable only via sub-requests. To expose signed fragment URLs (for ESI/hinclude) you enable framework.fragments (with a path like /_fragment) and framework.esi for ESI support. There is no twig.fragments key.

questions.q: By default, can a browser hit an embedded controller's fragment URL directly?

a.t: No — embedded controllers are exposed to direct URLs only when fragments are enabled, and the URL is signed
Yes — every embedded controller has a public URL automatically
No, direct fragment URLs are impossible in Symfony

questions.exp: Inline embedding uses internal sub-requests, not public URLs. Direct fragment access requires enabling framework.fragments, and Symfony signs the fragment URL (URI signer) so attackers cannot forge arbitrary controller calls. Assuming embeds are publicly routable is a security trap.

questions.q: What is the argument order of the `trans` filter?
questions.exp: The signature is message|trans(parameters = {}, domain = 'messages', locale = null).

questions.q: How do you pluralize a message in Symfony 8 templates?

a.t: Use ICU MessageFormat {count, plural, ...} in a +intl-icu domain

questions.exp: transchoice was removed; pluralization uses ICU MessageFormat, which is applied to catalogues whose domain ends with +intl-icu.

questions.q: A translation key has no entry for the current locale and no fallback. What is rendered?
questions.exp: The translator returns the untranslated message id when no translation is found.

questions.q: What replaced the removed transchoice() for count-based messages?

a.t: ICU MessageFormat plural syntax in a +intl-icu domain
The |transchoice filter, which is still available
A dedicated Pluralizer service you call in the controller

questions.exp: Both transchoice() and the |transchoice filter were removed. Pluralization is now expressed with ICU MessageFormat ({count, plural, one{...} other{...}}) in a +intl-icu domain. trans has no separate count argument — you pass count as an ICU parameter.

questions.q: Which catalogue file name enables ICU MessageFormat parsing for English?
questions.exp: A domain suffixed +intl-icu (e.g. messages+intl-icu.en.yaml) is parsed with the IntlFormatter, unlocking plural/select and locale-aware formatting. Putting ICU syntax in a plain messages.en.yaml file makes the braces render literally.

questions.q: After {% trans_default_domain 'admin' %}, what does {{ 'dashboard.title'|trans }} use?

a.t: The 'admin' domain, because trans_default_domain sets it for the rest of the template
The 'messages' domain, since the filter did not name one
It errors because a domain is required
The 'dashboard' domain, inferred from the key prefix

questions.exp: {% trans_default_domain 'admin' %} changes the default domain for the remainder of the template, so a trans call without an explicit domain uses 'admin'. Domains are never inferred from the key's dotted prefix.

questions.q: For the ICU message '{count, plural, =0 {none} one {# item} other {# items}}', what does count=1 render?
questions.exp: count=1 matches the CLDR 'one' category in English, and # inside the branch is replaced by the number, giving '1 item'. # prints the value (not a literal hash), 'one' is a category label not output, and =0 only matches the exact value 0.

questions.q: Which service does the Twig trans filter ultimately call?
questions.exp: TranslationExtension provides the trans filter/tag and delegates to TranslatorInterface::trans(), which loads catalogues, resolves the message, substitutes parameters, and runs ICU messages through the IntlFormatter.

questions.q: Where does #{...} string interpolation work in Twig?
questions.exp: The lexer only interpolates #{...} within double-quoted strings; single quotes render the text literally.

questions.q: What is the result of {{ 1 + 2 ~ 3 }}?
questions.exp: + binds tighter than ~, so (1 + 2) ~ 3 => 3 ~ 3 => the string "33".

questions.q: Which filter applies sprintf-style formatting in Twig?
questions.exp: The format filter wraps vsprintf, e.g. \"%s scored %d\"|format(a, b).

questions.q: Given {% set name = 'Ada' %}, what does {{ 'Hi #{name}' }} render?

a.t: Hi #{name} — single quotes are literal, so no interpolation happens
Hi Ada — interpolation works in any string
An error about #{ in a single-quoted string

questions.exp: Interpolation with #{...} works only in double-quoted strings. In a single-quoted literal the sequence is printed verbatim, so you get the raw text 'Hi #{name}'. Use double quotes ("Hi #{name}") for interpolation.

questions.q: What are the results of {{ "1" + "2" }} and {{ "1" ~ "2" }}?

a.t: 3 and "12" — + is numeric addition, ~ is string concatenation
An error, because + cannot be used on strings

questions.exp: In Twig, + is arithmetic addition (numeric strings are coerced), so "1" + "2" is 3. ~ concatenates after casting operands to string, so "1" ~ "2" is "12". Using + to "join" strings is a classic mistake.

questions.q: How does Twig implement #{...} interpolation internally?

a.t: It is a lexer feature: #{expr} in a double-quoted string is tokenised and compiled into ~ concatenation
It is a runtime str_replace over the rendered output
It calls PHP's built-in string interpolation on the template
It is a filter applied after escaping

questions.exp: Inside a "..." string the lexer detects #{, tokenises the embedded expression, and the parser compiles the whole literal into a ~ (string concatenation) chain — so "a #{x} b" becomes 'a ' ~ x ~ ' b'. It has nothing to do with PHP's own interpolation.

questions.q: Which filter performs keyed placeholder substitution like {{ '%who%'|replace({'%who%': name}) }}?
questions.exp: The replace filter takes a hash of search => replacement pairs and does keyed substitution, unlike format which uses positional sprintf placeholders. Translation strings commonly use this %name% placeholder style.

questions.q: What does asset('css/app.css') return?

a.t: A public URL/path (relative to public/) with base path and version applied

questions.exp: asset() resolves a path relative to public/ through the Symfony\Component\Asset\Packages service, applying base path and versioning.

questions.q: What is the purpose of asset versioning?

a.t: Cache busting so browsers refetch changed files

questions.exp: Versioning changes the URL when a file changes (static version or a JSON manifest of content hashes) so clients do not serve a stale cached copy.

questions.q: Which build tools are OUT of scope when only using asset()?
questions.exp: asset() only resolves the final public path/version. Bundling and hashing are done by AssetMapper or Webpack Encore, which are not covered here.

questions.q: Which service does the Twig asset() function delegate to?
questions.exp: AssetExtension wraps the Packages service. Each package pairs a base path/URL with a VersionStrategyInterface (Empty, Static, or JsonManifest), and Packages::getUrl() applies the version.

questions.q: How do you point image assets at a CDN while CSS stays local?

a.t: Define a named package with base_urls and call asset('img/x.png', 'cdn')
Hard-code the CDN URL in the template

questions.exp: framework.assets.packages lets you declare a named package (e.g. cdn with base_urls). asset('img/x.png', 'cdn') uses that package while the default package still serves CSS locally. There is no framework.assets.cdn flag.

questions.q: With a JSON manifest configured, what does asset('app.css') resolve to?

a.t: The content-hashed name looked up in manifest.json (e.g. app.7f3c.css), not the literal path
An error if app.css is not physically present

questions.exp: JsonManifestVersionStrategy maps the logical name to its hashed filename from manifest.json, so asset('app.css') returns the resolved hashed path. Expecting the literal path with a ?v query (that is StaticVersionStrategy) is the trap.

questions.q: True or false: you should use asset() to generate a link to a route-controlled page.

a.t: False — asset() is for static files under public/; use path()/url() for routes
True — asset() works for both routes and files

questions.exp: asset() only resolves a public file path (with base path + version); it does not know about routes. Route-controlled URLs come from path()/url() via the RoutingExtension. Swapping the two is a common confusion.

questions.q: What does {{ dump() }} with no arguments do?

a.t: Dumps all variables available in the current template context

questions.exp: Called with no arguments, dump() outputs the entire render context (all passed variables plus globals).

questions.q: Why does dump() error in the prod environment?

a.t: The DumpExtension is only registered in debug mode

questions.exp: The dump function/tag come from the debug-only DumpExtension (backed by VarDumper); in prod the function is undefined, so leftover dumps throw.

questions.q: What is the difference between {{ dump(x) }} and {% dump x %}?

a.t: The function prints inline; the tag sends data to the collector without injecting markup
The tag works in prod, the function does not
The function only works in prod

questions.exp: The dump() function outputs where called; the {% dump %} tag routes the data to the profiler/toolbar without adding markup to the page.

questions.q: What gives Symfony's dump() its rich, collapsible HTML output rather than plain var_dump?

a.t: Symfony's DumpExtension backed by VarDumper (VarCloner + HtmlDumper), replacing Twig's plain DebugExtension
Twig's core DebugExtension already produces collapsible HTML
PHP's native var_dump() with an ini setting

questions.exp: Twig core ships DebugExtension with a plain var_dump-based dump(). Symfony augments it with DumpExtension wired to VarDumper (VarCloner clones the variable, HtmlDumper renders collapsible, syntax-highlighted output and routes dumps to the toolbar). Cloning first also makes dumping large graphs safe (depth-limited).

questions.q: You add {% dump items %} but see nothing in the page HTML. Why?

a.t: The tag form intentionally injects no page markup; it sends data to the collector/toolbar
The tag only works in prod
items must be a scalar for {% dump %} to work
{% dump %} was removed; only dump() exists

questions.exp: Unlike the dump() function, the {% dump %} tag does not print inline — by design it routes the data to the dump destination (profiler/toolbar) so it does not pollute the page. Look in the web debug toolbar, not the page source.

questions.q: A deploy fails with 'Unknown "dump" function' on a page. What is the cause and fix?

a.t: A stray {{ dump() }} left in a template; dump is undefined in prod, so remove it
VarDumper is missing from require-dev; move it to require
The Twig cache is stale; clear it and dump will work in prod
dump was renamed in Symfony 8; use var_dump instead

questions.exp: dump tooling is registered only in debug mode, so a leftover dump() in a committed template throws 'Unknown "dump" function' in prod. The fix is to remove debug dumps before deploy (use logging/profiler in non-prod envs) — not to enable the extension in production.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are true about Twig syntax? (select all that apply)

a.t: {{ }} prints (and escapes) a value, {% %} executes logic without printing, {# #} is a comment
Filters bind tighter than arithmetic: {{ 1 + 2|abs }} is evaluated as 1 + (2|abs)
{% %} statements also print their result into the output
{% spaceless %} is still the recommended tag for stripping whitespace

questions.exp: The three delimiters split cleanly into print/do/comment: only {{ }} produces (escaped) output while {% %} never prints. // is floor division (7 // 2 gives 3, unlike / which yields a float), and filters have higher precedence than arithmetic operators, so 1 + 2|abs applies abs to 2 first. The standalone {% spaceless %} tag no longer exists — the modern form is {% apply spaceless %}.

questions.q: Which statements about Twig output escaping in Symfony are correct? (select all that apply)

a.t: The default escaping strategy is chosen from the template file extension, so a .txt.twig template escapes nothing
Escaping is applied when a value is printed with {{ }}, not when it is assigned with {% set %}
|raw and {% autoescape false %} disable protection, so they must only wrap trusted content
The html_attr strategy is just an alias of html and produces identical output
All templates always use the html strategy regardless of their extension
